name: Johnny Key
career_history: Principal Program Manager at Microsoft, 3/2025 to present; Director, Energy & Power Solutions at Freeport-McMoRan, 7/2019 to 2/2025; Manager of Energy Services at Freeport-McMoRan, 11/2013 to 6/2019; Chief Engineer - Energy Management at Freeport-McMoRan, 4/2011 to 11/2013; Fuel Engineer III at Arizona Public Service - APS, 10/2006 to 3/2011; Test Engineer II at Honeywell, 1/2005 to 10/2006

pipeline.project: Long Term Mapping - Utilities - Main List

biography: Johnny Key is at an inflection point in his career and is still sorting out what he wants. He is curious about the player, impact, and influence that the organization (Goodman Group) can have on reshaping the energy industry. He enjoys being part of the current moment reshaping the energy industry and sees this opportunity as aligned with that. He is interested in "tricky, nuanced work" and managing the narrative around the electric grid, especially as the data center world's narrative shifts. Johnny Key moved to Microsoft to take a step back from the responsibilities of leading a Fortune 500 global energy team. He is currently enjoying his role at Microsoft but acknowledges pros and cons. He works in regulatory strategy for energy markets and analytics, supporting the broader organization. He does not want to own a particular geography but acts as a support tool, advising others with his 15 years of experience. His expertise and strength lie in regulatory strategy, navigating the highly regulated utility world, and identifying levers and footholds for project execution. The organization's need is in data availability and data governance; Johnny Key helps with analytics to support the broader organization, including regulatory teams, by providing foundational data systems. The regulatory work Johnny Key does is within energy markets, and the analytics work is for a separate team, both reporting to one VP of energy. Johnny Key supports the team that handles the infrastructure side, including commercial aspects of dealing with utilities, transmission agreements, interconnection agreements, and determining construction responsibilities and payment. Johnny Key focuses on the nexus of analytics, performing analyses to understand project viability, and developing negotiation strategies and deal points. At Freeport, all of these responsibilities were within Johnny Key's scope, but in the current role, the aim is to leverage strengths without the responsibility of managing 40 employees. In the current role, Johnny Key is involved in regulatory engagement and interconnection agreements, focusing on providing expert advice and "muscle" to support those who own specific geographies, rather than being the primary lead on a particular geography. Johnny Key's current work involves understanding system impact studies and vetting assumptions to prevent punitive project outputs. While at Freeport, Johnny Key managed the full scope of activities. The current role at Microsoft is more tailored to advisory and support, focusing on specific strengths without the extensive management responsibilities of previous roles. Johnny Key's expertise lies in regulatory strategy and navigating the highly regulated utility world to execute projects. He supports teams handling transmission agreements and interconnection agreements by providing "muscle" and advice to those less experienced in fighting with utilities. In a previous role at Freeport, all aspects of regulatory engagement and interconnection agreements were within his scope. Johnny Key supports organizations with the "nexus of analytics," understanding whether a deal is good or bad, and developing negotiating strategies. He emphasizes that the "real path" through regulatory engagement and interconnection agreements requires an expert who understands the "why" and can vet assumptions in system impact studies to avoid punitive project outputs.
